newsitem.title: CANADA: Friedland sues U.S. government for C$150 million.
newsitem.headline: Friedland sues U.S. government for C$150 million.

text.p: Mining financier Robert Friedland said Tuesday he is suing the U.S. government for C$150 million in damages for seeking to seize part of his assets last summer.
Friedland said in a statement that any damages won would be donated to Canadian charities.

The lawsuit filed in Ontario Court on Monday claims the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency and Department of Justice "abused the processes of the U.S. and Canadian courts by making false allegations against Mr. Friedland and by withholding material information from the courts."
The suit also alleges Friedland was libelled by a U.S. Department of Justice press release.

The U.S. government last summer persuaded Canadian courts temporarily to freeze US$152 million worth of Friedland's holdings. It alleged Friedland was liable for the clean-up of a polluted mine site in Colorado. The Summitville mine had been owned by a company formerly headed by Friedland.
But the order impounding Friedland's assets was subsequently overturned by an Ontario court and the judge ruled that the U.S. government had misrepresented the facts.
